text:
Bell: Which bell is it?
Bell. The board has 10x10 sites (160x160 cells). The window shows one site; each move goes to the next site (up, down, left or right). One large bell hangs on a plain green board. Four parts sit in their places, each drawn as one big black shape filling one site (a part that sits at two or more sites shows the same shape at each of them): its hanging loop at the top: a black disc or a black triangle pointing up; the two ends of its rim at the lower left and lower right: a black triangle pointing down or a black square; two decorated bands side by side in the middle: a tall thin black bar or three flat black stripes; its clapper at the bottom: a black plus sign or a black diamond. Every other site shows plain green. The whole bell may sit one site higher, lower, left or right, or one site diagonally. Question: Which bell is it? The answer is one of eight bells, each with its own parts: aria = a black disc, a black triangle pointing down, a tall thin black bar, a black plus sign; cadenza = a black disc, a black triangle pointing down, three flat black stripes, a black diamond; coda = a black disc, a black square, a tall thin black bar, a black diamond; etude = a black disc, a black square, three flat black stripes, a black plus sign; fermata = a black triangle pointing up, a black triangle pointing down, a tall thin black bar, a black diamond; largo = a black triangle pointing up, a black triangle pointing down, three flat black stripes, a black plus sign; nocturne = a black triangle pointing up, a black square, a tall thin black bar, a black plus sign; sonata = a black triangle pointing up, a black square, three flat black stripes, a black diamond. Answer with its name. You may answer at any time; you do not need to see every site. Score: 20 if the answer is right, minus 10, minus 0.1 per move (movement budget 35).
The answers: 1 = aria, 2 = cadenza, 3 = coda, 4 = etude, 5 = fermata, 6 = largo, 7 = nocturne, 8 = sonata.
You see the board, 10 x 10 sites, only through a window of one site (16 x 16 cells). A move goes to the next site. At most 35 moves.
